channel.title: Andrew Edmond — Blog
channel.description: Notes on building and assessing AI-era software.

item.title: What shipping it taught me
item.description: The last note in the series — what held up (skills, invariants, truth as a build gate), what I'd do differently (instrument sooner, kill features faster), and the honest headline.

item.title: Twelve days with Apple's reviewers
item.description: The App Store review gauntlet round by round — a real defect, three AI questions answered by design, a caption edit — and why the standards, not the tooling, were the reason it survived.

item.title: The bug my wife found
item.description: A ducked-audio bug that survived multiple builds, the turn-taking fix, and the harder decision — retiring Lola's voice because the observed experience never fit.

item.title: Tests encode beliefs, and beliefs can be wrong at scale
item.description: The robots test the app — real magic-link sign-in, a 181-profile matrix in CI — and the night an audit found tests loyally protecting the wrong answers.

item.title: The funnel filed the complaints
item.description: First contact with real users — 1,200 views, two complete journeys, zero errors — and the funnel data that rebuilt the interview around one rule.

item.title: The code was correct. The platform didn't care.
item.description: Four production ops lessons from an AI build — in-memory counters on serverless, wide-open CORS defaults, a staging DB baked into prod, and dead source links.

item.title: The truth pipeline
item.description: How a three-step pipeline — source at scale, ground in primary sources, gate the build — turns hallucination from a prompt problem into a systems problem.

item.title: The walking skeleton
item.description: Why an ugly end-to-end walking skeleton beats polished fragments, and matters more with AI, not less — featuring the kitten Claude labeled "Madrid."

item.title: The most productive day was the day nothing got built
item.description: The four invariants behind Get Camino, set before any code was written, and how each one kept absorbing new surfaces as the product grew.

item.title: What makes an AI-built app "real"
item.description: The checklist I refused to ship without — real users, full pipelines, tests in CI, monitoring, rate limiting, security headers, and a citation on every claim.
